medium: H40 starts the interactive auto-HUD child before the explicit firmware mounts, ADSP/CDSP/SLPI sequence, and PID1 boot-chime worker. The HUD child can accept Bad Apple during that window; PID1 can then reset the shared audio status file and spawn a late chime worker after the demo pre-stop and audio worker launch. Because PID1 and the forked HUD have separate tracked-worker globals, the new PID binding does not serialize this cross-process late spawn. This preserves the boot-chime/menu race and invalidates the deterministic lifecycle hazard claim until boot prerequisites/chime complete before the HUD becomes interactive or an equivalent interprocess readiness/ownership gate is added and tested.
